item.title: Fired Journalists at Independent Military Publication Sue Pentagon
item.description: Three journalists dismissed from Stars and Stripes accused the government of violating their First Amendment rights, asking the courts to stop their termination.
item.dc:creator: Minho Kim
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:credit: Jared Soares for The New York Times
item.media:description: A lawsuit filed on Thursday argues that new Pentagon policies severely limit the editorial independence of Stars and Stripes, which started publishing during the Civil War.

item.title: In Trump’s Washington, Ballooning National Debt Stirs Little Action
item.description: The relative indifference to the news that the U.S. government now owes $40 trillion demonstrates how drastically the politics of deficit spending has changed.
item.dc:creator: Peter Baker
item.media:description: A sign showing the national debt last week at a bus stop in Washington.

item.title: Obama to Headline Fund-Raiser With Jeffries in New York
item.description: The top Democrats will gather party donors on Sept. 10, just as Republicans converge in Texas for their unusual midterm convention.
item.dc:creator: Shane Goldmacher
item.media:credit: The New York Times, left, Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: Representative Hakeem Jeffries and former President Barack Obama will aim to give Democrats a financial boost at a time when money is a concern for the party heading into the midterm elections.

item.title: Trump Signs Executive Order to Rename Lake Ontario to Lake America
item.description: The president also reiterated his criticism that Canada “treats us very badly.” Trade talks between the nations collapsed last week.
item.dc:creator: Erica L. Green
item.media:credit: Demetrius Freeman for The New York Times

item.title: C.I.A. Chief Delivered Bleak Assessment of Russia’s War in Secretive Moscow Visit
item.description: John Ratcliffe’s meeting this week with a Russian intelligence chief was aimed at pushing the Kremlin to pursue a peace deal with Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: Adam Entous and Julian E. Barnes
item.media:description: John Ratcliffe, the C.I.A. director, delivered an urgent message to Aleksandr V. Bortnikov, the head of Russia’s F.S.B. intelligence service this week in a secret visit to Moscow.

item.title: DeSantis Administration Misspent $10 Million, Grand Jury Says
item.description: A charity tied to Gov. Ron DeSantis’s wife received the money from a state Medicaid settlement and diverted it to political committees supporting a cause favored by the governor.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Mazzei and David Ovalle
item.media:description: Casey DeSantis, Florida’s first lady, started the Hope Florida charity in 2021 and made it central to her public persona.

item.title: Secrecy in Lawsuits Has ‘Run Amok,’ Scholars Say
item.description: Two recent studies say judges are not doing enough to protect the public interest in openness.
item.dc:creator: Adam Liptak
item.category: White House East Wing and Ballroom (Washington, DC)
item.media:description: The U.S. Supreme Court in June.

item.title: Trump Administration to Expand Deportation Flights to Haiti
item.description: Flights to the Caribbean nation will increase from once a month to once a week now that the Supreme Court allowed President Trump to cancel a humanitarian program.
item.dc:creator: Hamed Aleaziz, Zolan Kanno-Youngs and Frances Robles
item.media:description: Deportation flights to Haiti will increase as soon as this week.

item.title: Trump Raises Money in Texas With Control of the Senate in the Balance
item.description: Many Republicans are hoping for financial support from President Trump, whose fund-raising power in the party remains unmatched despite his low poll numbers.
item.dc:creator: Luke Broadwater
item.media:credit: Meridith Kohut for The New York Times
item.media:description: A cutout of President Trump in Cypress, Texas, during the Republican primary runoff for Senate between Attorney General Ken Paxton and Senator John Cornyn in May.

item.title: U.S. to Withdraw 200 Troops Sent to Nigeria Under Trump
item.description: Officials say the small, limited deployment could serve as a model. But terrorists in the country have continued to attack and kill.
item.dc:creator: Eric Schmitt, Saikou Jammeh and Ismail Auwal
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:description: Nigerian soldiers took part in a search-and-rescue exercise at the Maiduguri Air Force Base earlier this month. Nigerian forces worked with the American military to kill one of the Islamic State’s highest-ranking leaders.

item.title: Starbucks Drops Drink Powder That Enveloped Baristas in Clouds of Dust
item.description: Baristas said the ingredient left them coughing and sneezing.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Davis O’Brien and Julie Creswell
item.media:description: A Starbucks store in Austin, Texas, this month. The company this week removed a powder used in its blended refreshers drinks from its U.S. stores.

item.title: Jury Begins Deliberations in Lindsay Clancy Murder Trial
item.description: In closing arguments, Ms. Clancy’s lawyer called her “a darn good mother.” The prosecutor accused her of “extreme atrocity and cruelty.”
item.dc:creator: Jacey Fortin and Maia Spoto
item.media:description: Lindsay Clancy in court during her murder trial on Wednesday in Plymouth, Mass.

item.title: ICE agent Christian Castro Released From Texas Jail After Minnesota Loses Court Fight
item.description: The state had sought to have the agent extradited from Texas to answer charges in Minneapolis related to an on-duty shooting that wounded an immigrant.
item.dc:creator: Mitch Smith and Ernesto Londoño
item.media:description: Christian Castro was one of thousands of agents sent to Minnesota in the winter as part of the Trump administration’s deportation campaign.

item.title: Democrats to Force Senate Vote on Israel’s Human Rights Practices
item.description: Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland is leading a group of Democrats seeking answers about violence against Palestinians in the Israeli-occupied West Bank.
item.dc:creator: Robert Jimison
item.category: Human Rights and Human Rights Violations
item.media:description: A handcuffed Palestinian man being detained by Israeli border police officers during an army operation in the Qalandiya refugee camp in the West Bank on Tuesday.

item.title: Trump’s Strength in Primaries is Clear. The Midterms Pose a Different Test.
item.description: The president’s pull with the party base has been clear and his resources are vast. But his low approval ratings make him a liability with swing voters.
item.dc:creator: Tim Balk, Shane Goldmacher and Maggie Haberman
item.media:credit: Bryan Anselm for The New York Times
item.media:description: President Trump campaigning with Representative Mike Lawler of New York in May. Republicans have to weigh Mr. Trump’s approval ratings against his popularity among his base.

item.title: Judge Allows Option of Manslaughter Verdict in Lindsay Clancy Case
item.description: If jurors find Ms. Clancy guilty in the strangling deaths of her three children, they will choose among first-degree murder, second-degree murder and manslaughter.
item.dc:creator: Maia Spoto and Jenna Russell
item.media:description: Lindsay Clancy is on trial for the strangling deaths of her three children.

item.title: He Thought He Destroyed a Flock Camera, but It Was a Decoy, Police Say
item.description: A Florida man was charged over the vandalism of a decoy version of the automated license plate readers, the authorities said.
item.dc:creator: Neil Vigdor
item.media:description: A Flock camera on a street in Massachusetts. The cameras and related technology have faced a backlash over privacy and misuse.

item.title: Administration Lawyer Chosen to Lead Panel Considering Trump Construction Projects
item.description: Mark Paoletta, also a close associate of Justice Clarence Thomas’s, has been named by President Trump to lead the National Capital Planning Commission.
item.dc:creator: Luke Broadwater
item.media:credit: Tierney L. Cross/The New York Times
item.media:description: As the chairman of the National Capital Planning Commission, Mark Paoletta will be tasked with vetting President Trump’s planned arch and other construction projects.

item.title: State Department Advances Trump Crackdown on ‘Far-Left Terrorism’
item.description: Critics say the Trump administration’s focus is disproportionate, as analysts raise alarms about the growing strength of far-right movements.
item.dc:creator: Michael Crowley
item.media:credit: Saher Alghorra for The New York Times
item.media:description: An encampment of displaced Palestinians in February, surrounded by destroyed buildings in Gaza City.

item.title: West Point Climate Professor Says He Was Fired for Refusing to ‘Defy Science’
item.description: Dr. Adam Kalkstein is suing the U. S. Military Academy, where he was a professor of geography and the only climate scientist, after being fired.
item.dc:creator: Michael C. Bender and Greg Jaffe
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:description: Cadets walking near Pershing Barracks at the U.S. Military Academy at West Point in 2014. A West Point climate professor says he was fired for refusing to “defy science.”

item.title: New White House Counsel Isn’t a Yes Man, but He Won’t Say No, Either
item.description: Will Scharf has proved his loyalty to President Trump, even filming a TV ad in which he blows away documents from the president’s legal cases. His new role will be to provide in-house legal advice.
item.dc:creator: Luke Broadwater
item.media:description: Will Scharf in the Oval Office earlier this month.

item.title: Justice Dept. Charges Owner of Failed Surrogacy Firm With Fraud
item.description: The owner of Surro Connections is accused of stealing over $1 million from prospective parents and using it to pay off gambling debts, take trips and purchase luxury goods.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Kliff
item.media:credit: Eric Lee for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Justice Department filed charges against the owner of Surro Connections, a surrogacy firm in Washington State.

item.title: Secret Service Officials Said to Be Put on Leave Amid Internal Inquiry
item.description: The agency’s top spokesman is among those on leave, according to two Trump administration officials. The agency said three people faced a misconduct investigation.
item.dc:creator: Maggie Haberman, Zolan Kanno-Youngs and Kate Kelly
item.media:description: The Secret Service has been under intense scrutiny for years, particularly after two attempts on Donald J. Trump’s life in 2024.

item.title: Man Accused of Bringing Guillotine to D.C. Is Arrested
item.description: Philan-Tam-Duy Le, 35, of Julian, Calif., was taken into custody for “being in possession of the guillotine,” the police said.
